To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of population and economic activity in the United States has become increasingly uneven, and that the unevenness is increasing over time, but that the distributional changes are not uniform over the nation, nor are they uniform across the major sectors of the economy.

the spatial structure of the United States is highly fragmented, that this fragmentation has been increasing over the past two decades, and that this fragmentation is associated with a number of negative consequences, such as increased social costs of commuting, greater environmental degradation, and higher levels of crime.

the spatial structure of the U.S. is not optimal, that the spatial structure is not static, that the spatial system is complex, that the structure of the system is not understood, and that the structure of our system has a significant impact on our lives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a comprehensive spatial policy framework that will enhance our ability to achieve national goals.
the spatial distribution and redistribution patterns of population, employment, and income in the U.S. and the implications of these patterns for public policy.
developing and applying a spatial policy framework that can be used to guide the formulation of policies that influence the distribution and redistribution of people, activities, and resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have not developed an adequate understanding of the dynamics of spatial systems and, consequently, we have not been able to formulate effective policies to influence the distribution of population and economic activity.
we still lack a national strategy of urbanization, and the reasons are the same as those identified by Alonso in 1972.
we still have a poor understanding of the spatial distribution of people, activities, and resources in the United States.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have a better understanding of the spatial distribution of economic activities and population, but we have not been able to develop a comprehensive policy framework for dealing with the issues that have emerged as a result of our increased understanding.
the spatial policy framework has not been enhanced with ecological analysis.

we have learned much about spatial distribution and redistribution in the United States, but we have not yet integrated that knowledge into the policy framework that is used to make decisions about the spatial organization of society.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of population and economic activity is a system of systems.

we must develop a more comprehensive and integrated understanding of how spatial distributions are formed, and how they change, in order to develop more effective distributional policies and to avoid unintended consequences.
the spatial organization of a nation’s population and economy is a complex, dynamic system that is not well understood.
